transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, it’s really nice to meet you too. Um... well, I hope I'm in the right place for this. I feel a little silly even bringing it up, honestly, but... I guess I've just been having some trouble staying on track with my work. 

I'm a secondary school teacher, and I really do care about my students and my job, but... well, for example, I’ll sit down with a stack of essays to grade, or a new curriculum document, and I fully intend to just get to work. I really do want to do it. But then... maybe ten minutes later, I’ll realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page the whole time. My mind will be off thinking about three other completely different things, and I’m barely taking in a single word of what’s right in front of me. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, because as a teacher I feel like I should just be able to sit down and focus. Um, does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay...
When you were a child, did you also have a hard time paying attention or staying on task?

Oh, um... well, I was a pretty good kid overall, I think. I wasn't a troublemaker or anything like that. But, um... I guess if I really think back to primary school, yeah, maybe a little bit? 

It's actually a bit embarrassing, but my parents were always finding these crumpled-up worksheets buried at the bottom of my backpack that I had just completely forgotten to turn in. And, um, my report cards were usually mostly positive, but the teachers would always write things like... well, they'd say I was "bright but careless," or that I wouldn't really finish my work unless I was being closely supervised. 

I always meant to do the work, I promise, I just... I don't know, got sidetracked easily, I suppose. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm giving you the right information...
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when you don’t want to?

Oh, um... no, I don't really think I do. I mean, aside from the normal things, like... you know, hoping I get all my grading done on time and wanting to do a good job for my students. But I wouldn't say I'm a worrier, really. 

If anything, I'm usually pretty... well, pretty easygoing. My friends would probably say I'm pretty relaxed overall. Sometimes I almost feel like I actually *should* worry a little bit more about my deadlines and things, to be honest! But no, I don't really find myself just sitting around stressing over different things out of nowhere. 

Um, does that make sense? I hope that's a helpful answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Did these focus problems start after a specific stressful change or event in your life?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it was a single stressful event, exactly. Like, nothing terrible happened or anything! But... I guess things did get a bit more difficult for me about, hmm, maybe 11 months ago? 

The school made some changes to the curriculum calendar, which is totally normal, of course. But they also added these mandatory after-school planning meetings. And, um, I really want to be a team player and contribute, but since then... I don't know, it just feels like my brain has been having a much harder time keeping up with everything. It's definitely been noticeably worse since those changes started. 

I feel a bit bad complaining about it, because all the other teachers seem to be handling the new schedule just fine. I really should be able to manage it too, you know? Um, is that the sort of timeline you were looking for? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be...
Do you also have this same kind of trouble focusing in other parts of your life besides work?

Oh, um... well, I suppose it's not just at school, if I'm being completely honest. I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly everywhere, but... yeah, it does bleed over into home life a bit. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but my wife has sort of had to take over paying the bills and keeping track of all our appointments and reminders. I always have the best intentions, I really do, but she just... well, she realized she couldn't really count on me to remember those things. She's been incredibly patient about it, though! I'm very lucky.

And, um, I guess I should probably mention... at work, it's gotten to the point where my department chair actually put me on a, um, a support plan. Just because of the missed follow-throughs and things. They framed it as a positive thing, just to help me succeed, but... I know it means I haven't been doing as well as I should be. 

I hope it's okay that I'm sharing all this... I just want to make sure you have the full picture. Does that help answer your question?
